cli.runtime.reconciliation: Reconciliation page completed: {count} outcomes. Task acceptance is unchanged.
cli.runtime.idleShutdown: No request or execution for {duration} (hh:mm:ss): this automatically started service is stopping.
cli.runtime.shutdownAdmitted: Runtime service {serviceId} (instance {instanceId}): shutdown accepted; it is stopping now.
cli.secret.store.envMissing: Config references available from env but missing in {to}: {names}.
cli.secret.store.envPrompt: Switch anyway? These references will stop resolving. [yes/no]
cli.secret.store.pickTitle: Choose the key store (now: {current}). Keys are moved, checked, then removed from the old store.
cli.secret.store.downgradePrompt: Moving keys from {from} to {to} lowers how they are protected on disk.
cli.pool.drift: POOL_ADMISSION_CAPACITY_DRIFT: pool {pool}, {source} requests {requestedExecution}/{requestedInFlight}, pool capacity {execution}/{inFlight}. Set pool capacity explicitly.
doctor.poolReadiness.evidence: Pool readiness: {status} (pool {pool}, capacity {execution}/{inFlight}: running / including evaluation)
cli.audit.rebaseline.done: Audit {scope} re-baselined: checkpoint {sequence} over audit head {head}. Export a new witness with deckent audit verify --export-checkpoint.
error.BACKUP_SET_NOT_FOUND: No recovery set at {path}: the path does not exist or holds no recovery set (a set is one folder with MANIFEST.sha256 in it). Nothing was read or changed. Check the path; scheduled sets are kept under the installation's state/backups/recovery folder by default.
error.BACKUP_SET_UNREADABLE: This user cannot read the recovery set {path} (permission denied); nothing was changed. As the owner of the set, allow reading (chmod 700 on the folder, chmod 600 on its files), then rerun the same command.
error.BACKUP_PASSPHRASE_REQUIRED: No passphrase was given, so the set was not opened. Type it at the hidden prompt in a terminal or pipe it on standard input (never as an argument), then rerun the same command.
error.BACKUP_MANIFEST_INVALID: The recovery set was modified: its files no longer match its manifest, so it is not used. Nothing was restored or changed; use another set.
cli.pool.view.held: Pool {pool} · on hold: no new work starts
cli.pool.view.drained: Drained: no work is left running in this pool.
cli.pool.view.capacity: Capacity: at most {slots} jobs at the same time (this machine suggests {recommended} — deckent doctor)
cli.pool.view.capacityEvaluating: Capacity: at most {slots} jobs running and {inFlight} including evaluation at the same time (this machine suggests {recommended} — deckent doctor)
cli.pool.capacityUnchanged: Pool {pool} already has capacity {execution}/{inFlight}; nothing changed.
cli.pool.card.holdWhat: No new work starts in this pool; work already running finishes.
cli.pool.card.resumeWhat: Waiting work in this pool may start again.
cli.pool.card.setCapacity: Set capacity to {slots} running / {inFlight} including evaluation?
cli.pool.card.setCapacityWhat: Applies to the next work the pool admits; running work is not stopped.
cli.pool.card.slotsTitle: How many jobs may run at the same time?
cli.pool.card.quotaRelease: Release the jobs waiting on channel {channel}?
cli.pool.card.quotaReleaseWhat: Jobs parked on this channel's quota may start again now.
cli.backup.list.title: Recovery sets in {directory}
cli.backup.list.schedule: Schedule: {schedule} · keeps the newest {retention} scheduled sets
cli.backup.list.passphraseHere: The backup passphrase is stored inside this installation; keep a copy off this machine as well.
cli.backup.list.empty: No recovery set here yet. Make one: deckent backup create --scope <scope> --set <path>
cli.backup.list.elsewhere: Only this folder is listed; sets made elsewhere with --set are not shown.
cli.backup.list.column.name: Name
cli.backup.card.restoreService: Runtime service: stopped (a restore never runs next to a running service).
cli.backup.card.restoreKept: Every file it replaces is kept next to it as <name>.damaged-<id>; nothing is deleted.
cli.backup.done.verify: Backup verified: {set} is authentic ({files} files, made {made}).
cli.backup.done.preserved: Replaced files kept next to them: {paths}
error.BACKUP_SET_REQUIRED: {action} needs the recovery set: add --set <path>. Sets in the default folder: {sets}. List them with: deckent backup
error.BACKUP_PASSPHRASE_PROMPT_UNAVAILAB: This terminal cannot hide typing, so the passphrase was not asked. Pipe it on standard input instead (never as an argument) and rerun.
cli.secret.list.title: Secrets in {store}: {count} stored. Values are never shown.
cli.secret.list.empty: No secret is stored or referenced yet.
cli.secret.list.never: Add or change one: deckent secret set <NAME> (value from a hidden prompt or stdin).
cli.secret.list.column.name: Name
cli.secret.card.setTitle: Which key to store? (referenced by the config, not in the store yet)
cli.secret.card.deleteUsers: Still used by: {users}. They stop working until it is set again.
cli.secret.card.deleteUnused: Nothing in the config references it.
error.SECRET_NAME_REQUIRED: Every key the config references is already stored, so there is nothing to pick. Name the key: deckent secret set <NAME>.
cli.secret.store.howTo: Change it: deckent secret store (a picker on a terminal) or deckent secret store --to <store> --scope <scope>.
cli.secret.store.note.env: read from the service's environment; Deckent cannot store keys here
cli.secret.store.note.file: plain text on disk, readable only by you; less safe
cli.secret.store.note.encryptedFile: encrypted on disk; its opening key is in the same folder
cli.secret.store.note.other: a store added by an extension
cli.secret.store.downgradeTitle: Lower the protection of your keys?
cli.secret.store.envTitle: Switch although some references would stop resolving?
cli.secret.store.done.current: {store} is already the current store; nothing changed.
cli.secret.store.done.notCleaned: the old store still holds copies (deckent doctor shows them).
cli.audit.limit: This check catches a change made from the same account; it does not prevent one. For full assurance keep the checkpoint off this machine: deckent audit verify --export-checkpoint <file>
cli.audit.exported: Checkpoint {sequence} saved: {path}. Keep this file off this machine.
error.AUDIT_CHECKPOINT_EXPORT_EMPTY: There is no checkpoint to export yet; nothing was written.
error.AUDIT_CHECKPOINT_EXPORT_EXISTS: {path} already exists; it was not overwritten. Name a new file.
error.AUDIT_CHECKPOINT_EXPORT_FAILED: The checkpoint could not be written to {path}; check that the folder exists and is writable.
cli.runtime.status.buildOther: build {commit} (this CLI is {own}; deckent runtime restart moves the service to it)
cli.runtime.status.config.stale: Configuration: changed since the service started — deckent runtime restart applies it
cli.runtime.status.config.unknown: Configuration: cannot tell (this service does not report it)
cli.runtime.status.workUnknown: Running work: cannot be read now
cli.runtime.status.serviceUnconfigured: Service without a configured identity · instance {instance} · {started}
cli.runtime.status.idle: Stops by itself after {duration} without work
cli.runtime.status.stopped: Runtime service: not running. It starts by itself when you open deckent; deckent runtime serve runs it in the foreground.
cli.runtime.card.work: Affected work now: {running} running, {evaluating} being evaluated (scope {scope})
cli.runtime.card.effect: Stopping never cancels worker operations; requests still open after the grace period are reported as incomplete and recovery runs at the next start.
cli.runtime.card.restartEffect: It then starts again from the current build and configuration.
error.RUNTIME_SHUTDOWN_REASON_REQUIRED: Say why the service stops: add --reason <text> (it is audited). A person on a terminal confirms on a card instead.
cli.toolchains.network.on: Checks the newest versions over the network ({endpoint}).
cli.toolchains.network.off: The version check is off (toolchains.currency.mode off); no network is used.
cli.toolchains.empty: No worker toolchain is in use.
cli.toolchains.allCurrent: Every tool in use is current.
cli.toolchains.auto.on: Automatic update: on — the service builds a new worker image when a tool is out of date (checks every {interval}); new Runs use it.
cli.toolchains.auto.propose: Automatic update: proposal only — deckent toolchains update builds it after you confirm.
cli.toolchains.update.disabled: Toolchain updates are off (toolchains.update.mode off); nothing was planned.
cli.toolchains.update.noChange: Every tool is current; no new worker image is needed.
cli.toolchains.update.applyHint: Nothing was built. deckent toolchains update --apply builds it (Docker).
cli.toolchains.update.built: Built worker image {version} ({image}). Profile change proposal: {proposal} — the installation's profiles are not changed here.
cli.toolchains.card.title: Build worker image {version}?
cli.toolchains.card.build: Builds a Docker image; it may take up to {limit} (toolchains.update.buildTimeoutMs).
cli.toolchains.card.running: Running work keeps its current image; this writes a profile proposal and changes no profile.
cli.toolchains.card.building: Building the worker image (Docker; up to {limit})…
cli.paths.title: Paths of the installation in {root}
cli.paths.titleGlobal: Paths of this user's global installation in {root}
cli.paths.socketWhy: The service listens on the short /tmp socket: a Unix socket path holds at most 108 bytes, so the layout path only names it.
cli.paths.socketUnknown: The socket the service really uses is shown by deckent doctor.
cli.paths.resource.autonomyShadow: delivery autonomy shadow records (rule off, advice only)
cli.paths.resource.memoryPurges: memory purge journal (kept across a backup restore, re-applied before work starts)
cli.paths.resource.brainWaits: active Brain quota waits before a Run exists (removed when the wait ends; not evidence)
cli.paths.resource.headlessLogins: Brain login root (one folder per CLI; never in a backup)
cli.paths.resource.signers: signer keys (private keys of enrolled AI principals, never backed up) and the revocation log
error.SECRET_SET_TERMINAL_REQUIRED: A key is stored only from a person's terminal, at the hidden prompt: a piped, scripted or agent call is refused before the key is read, and nothing was stored. Run it on your terminal: deckent secret set <NAME>.
cli.backup.list.passphraseUnknown: Whether the backup passphrase is stored inside this installation: unknown (the secret store could not be read for you now).
cli.secret.card.grantTitle: Use the main key {name} in the project {project}?
cli.secret.card.revokeTitle: Stop using the main key {name} in the project {project}?
cli.secret.card.grantBody: The value stays in the main vault; only this project may use it. The decision is recorded in the audit log first. AI sessions cannot answer this card.
cli.secret.card.handoverTitle: Move the project key vault to {project}? (only when the original folder is gone)
cli.secret.card.vaultMain: main vault (the installation; other projects can use it only with a grant)
cli.secret.card.vaultProject: this project's own vault (used only here; declare it in .deck as NAME=project)
cli.secret.done.granted: {name} (main vault) may now be used in {project}.
cli.secret.done.revoked: {name} (main vault) is no longer granted to {project}.
cli.secret.done.handedOver: The project key vault now belongs to {project}.
cli.secret.done.setProject: {name} saved in the project vault of {project}. Declare it in .deck as {name}=project to use it.
cli.secret.done.deletedProject: {name} removed from the project vault of {project}.
cli.secret.inventory.title: Keys of {project} (main vault: {store}). Values are never shown.
cli.secret.inventory.titleAll: Keys of every project of this main vault ({store}); this project: {project}. Values are never shown.
cli.secret.inventory.finding.grantRequir: {name} is used but not granted to {project}: deckent secret grant {name} --scope <scope>
cli.secret.inventory.finding.undeclared: {name} is in the project vault of {project} but .deck does not declare it: add {name}=project to .deck
cli.secret.inventory.finding.declaredMis: {name} is declared in .deck of {project} but not stored: deckent secret set {name} --main or --project
cli.secret.inventory.never: Store: deckent secret set <NAME> --main|--project. Lend a main key to this project: deckent secret grant <NAME> --scope <scope>.
cli.uninstall.title: Uninstall Deckent
cli.uninstall.packageHandoff: After exit, if no other installation uses it: {command}
cli.uninstall.packageUnknown: Package kept. Verify the installation method before removing the shared package.
cli.uninstall.status.noop: No eligible owned resources remain to remove.
cli.uninstall.status.cancelled: Removal cancelled. Check the per-item outcomes and any prepared backup.
cli.uninstall.status.partial: Removal is incomplete. Review the retained evidence before continuing.
cli.uninstall.status.unknown: Outcome unknown. Reconcile the retained effect before continuing.
cli.uninstall.reason.durable: Durable data is kept by default
cli.uninstall.reason.protected-session: Protected session stays with its owner
cli.uninstall.reason.service-unresolved: Service ownership or activity is unresolved
cli.uninstall.purge.confirm: Yes, delete only the listed backed-up global data
cli.uninstall.retainedData: Project .deckent/ folders are always kept. Global data is kept by default; use --purge to preview its backed-up removal. Unlisted or shared resources are also kept.
cli.uninstall.reinstall: To reinstall, use the original package manager and run deckent in your project folder. Retained project data is reused.
cli.uninstall.blocker.backup-destination: Complete verified backup coverage and a destination outside the removal roots are required. Global data stays.
